With these assumptions, the main difference between the R134a and ammonia cases for a single equipment configuration is the slightly higher capital cost and the associated real levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) for R134a systems because they require larger refrigerant piping and pumps. 18 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 4.5 Limitations of this Study Regulatory frameworks specifically tailored for OTEC systems are currently absent; however, many existing oil and gas-relevant regulations concerning subsea equipment and Coast Guard requirements for vessels are assumed to be directly applicable. The primary distinction is that OTEC equipment does not handle produced fluids. Nonetheless, some components near the platform would contain refrigerants, which are not currently addressed in these regulations. Additionally, the service life of existing facilities may constrain potential sites for collocation. While this study is primarily focused on collocation with newly deployed facilities, it should be noted that there are precedents, such as the Auger platform, where facilities have undergone life extensions, significantly surpassing the originally anticipated 20-year lifespan, making them potential candidate for future consideration for addition of an OTEC plant. Additionally, the fact that offshore costs of any system installation and maintenance far surpass that of their onshore equivalents. While the authors made their best attempts to correctly reflect operation and maintenance efforts and costs for the presented OTEC concepts, it is likely that they may be underestimated. 5 Synergies Besides the potential reduction in fuel gas usage and its associated revenue increase and GHG reduction potential, OTEC power can reduce the reliance on diesel fuel during periods when production is unavailable (e.g., during planned or unplanned shutdowns). It may also provide essential power during the period of time immediately following an unplanned platform power outage in cases where it is safe to continue providing power to essential systems and/or living spaces. The detailed design of the electrical system and the load shedding priorities would need to incorporate the power supply from the OTEC system. 5.1 Industrial Cooling from Cold Water Intake Another potential synergy between oil and gas production and the OTEC equipment is the possible use of the OTEC cold water supply in process cooling applications. For example, since the cold water considered in this case is at around 5 °C, using this water to cool compressor discharge or to cool well fluids in cases where the boarding temperatures are high can be worthwhile use cases to consider in planning for coupled OTEC and platform designs. In addition, cold seawater systems have been used on land for air conditioning in office buildings and may be able to displace or supplement the traditional A/C in the living quarters and other enclosed human environments on the platform. While these 19 OESI 2.0 M-1 T-1-P1.1 – Objective 3 Report April 2025 applications were not evaluated as part of this study, they were deemed worthy of mention due to their synergistic potential. 6
